THE RESTATEMENTS: tools/restate.py holds a fixed, named registry; each restatement states why it preserves meaning, applies only where that reason holds (a restatement that cannot prove preservation for a case declines that case and says why), is deterministic, and never changes the original object; each has a test showing it changes the bytes yet not the meaning on worked examples, and a test that it declines where it must (for example, an id rename that would collide with an existing id; a numeric rewrite on a field the schema types as an integer count). The registry includes at least: consistent step-id renaming through uses and bind; packet dict key reordering; equality side swap; expression whitespace; schema-typed numeric literal rewriting.

THE AUDIT: tools/restatement_audit.py applies every applicable restatement to all 1,796 benchmark cases (through the path the benchmark uses) and to every derivation-tier row (through the path its source used), and compares, by canonical form, the verdict, each step's status, and broken_at, gap_at and error_at against the unrestated run; it runs under halt_telemetry's isolation (imported: memo off, temporary stores, a copy of data/ for reference reads), warms the verifiers first, re-measures a verifier timeout once and never retries until it passes; it reports, by domain, by restatement and by case, every change and every decline; it exits 1 on any HOLDS/BROKEN flip, 2 if it measured nothing, else 0; tests prove the exit paths with planted defects (a monkeypatched verifier that flips under one restatement; one that turns HOLDS into INCOMPLETE; a restatement that is planted to change meaning must be caught by its own preservation test, not by the audit).
NO WRITES: a subprocess test hash-compares the stores the tool is pointed at, as halt_telemetry's does.

RECORDED: MEASURED.md gains a section with the audit's output at the run's last commit - cases and rows audited, restatements applied and declined, every change named by domain, restatement and case, HOLDS/BROKEN flips (expected 0; any found is listed first and is the loop's next run), the other changes as wants - with the command that reproduces each number, the product line (finds verifier defects before users do; never a verdict path), and a test that recomputes every quoted number from the tool (fast part in the suite, the benchmark-wide part behind -m slow if it would breach the 60 s budget on CI).

goal: Measurement 4 of the TRM report (C:\Users\hdven\OneDrive\Desktop\reports\Tiny recursive models and the kernel.md): adapt TRM's augmentation voting into an AUDIT OF THE VERIFIERS, never a vote. A claim restated in a way that provably preserves its meaning must get the same verdict; a verdict that changes under such a restatement is a verifier defect, named and filed, and a HOLDS-to-BROKEN or BROKEN-to-HOLDS flip is the critical kind. Agreement under restatement is never used to raise or lower any verdict, and nothing in src/ reads the audit. A fixed registry of restatements, tools/restate.py, each defined with the reason it preserves meaning and pinned by a test that it does (for example: a derivation's step ids renamed consistently through every uses and bind reference; the keys of every packet dict reordered; an equality's two sides swapped; whitespace in an expression string varied; a numeric field's literal rewritten only where the generated schema types the field so that the rewrite cannot change it), and an audit tool, tools/restatement_audit.py, that applies every applicable restatement to every benchmark case and every derivation-tier row and compares the verdict, each step's status and the trail's pointers against the original. It reports every change by domain, by restatement and by case, exits nonzero on any HOLDS/BROKEN flip, and names everything else as a want. Its measured output and the wants are recorded in MEASURED.md. Fixing any defect it finds is not this run; each becomes its own run in the loop. Tools, tests and MEASURED.md only: nothing deploys. The run starts after 2026-11-03-topological-order is recorded; its branch is restatement-audit.

findings: THE RESTATEMENTS, numeric literal rewriting: there is no type source, so the restatement is either vacuous or unsafe. The audit passes Python objects, never JSON text (benchmark.py:276; the tier's fixtures), and 0.05 and 5e-2 are the same float there. So the only rewrite that reaches a verifier changes the type, int to float. And schema.py:160 types every field as ['number', 'string', 'boolean', 'array', 'object'], so 'only where the generated schema types the field so that the rewrite cannot change it' never holds. The decline example 'a field the schema types as an integer count' names a type the schema never produces. Measured at origin/main 06a78d2 (scratch export, memo off, temporary stores), a naive int-to-float over the 837 benchmark cases holding an int gives 2 HOLDS-to-BROKEN flips: golden:pressure_fighting:true and check:pressure_fighting.observation:true. In both, PFS_VERIFY.observation.frame_seq goes from 1 to 1.0 and the verifier answers 'frame_seq must be an integer >= 1' (pressure_fighting.py:92). The schema types frame_seq as any type. Drop this restatement, or name a type source that a test pins per field (for example, fields the verifier reads only through float()), and decline every field it cannot type.

THE RESTATEMENTS, step-id renaming: it never reaches a verifier and its preservation cases are unhandled. verify_step receives only (domain, spec) (derivation.py:789). On the benchmark it cannot apply to the 60 claims, because derivation.verify fixes the id 'b' (:921). On the 1,736 single-step cases it changes only names. So it audits derivation.py's id resolution on the tier, not the verifiers, and the record must count it that way. To preserve meaning it must: rename by str(id) (ids are coerced at :648); treat a falsy id (0 or '') as its default s{i}; rename a default-id step by giving it an explicit id; rename every carrier of a repeated id alike, and decline any rename that creates or removes a collision. DEFAULT_ID_COLLISION's explicit s1 and default s1 are one repeated id, so renaming one of them resolves b's bind. It must refuse a new id containing '.', since a bind ref splits at the first '.' (:668); rewrite the bind ref's source part and a document's {step_id} text references (compose hashes the text, compose.py:55-64); and compare broken_at, gap_at and error_at through the rename map. As written, every renamed row with a pointer reads as a change.

THE RESTATEMENTS, what proves preservation: 'changes the bytes yet not the meaning on worked examples' names no oracle. If meaning is judged by running the verifiers, the preservation test is the audit on a few examples. It then blames a verifier defect on the restatement, and passes a meaning-changing restatement that today's verifiers happen to tolerate. In that case 'caught by its own preservation test, not by the audit' proves nothing. Require each preservation test to decide meaning without calling any verifier, by an oracle named per restatement: key reordering, validate.canonical_json_bytes equal; equality swap, the two parsed sides exchanged (srepr equal pairwise) with every other field unchanged; whitespace, inserted only between Python tokens (the tokenize sequence and ast.dump unchanged), and declining when the size guard would trip (the 4,000-character json.dumps(params) bound, derivation.py:142 and :241); id rename, the derivation's id graph isomorphic under the map. Require too a test that preservation tests import nothing from concordance.verifiers.

THE AUDIT, what is compared: verdict, step status and pointers leave out refutations and read, which per CLAUDE.md travel with every verdict and into the seal. A restatement under which one of a verifier's checks silently becomes not_applicable while another still confirms leaves the status CONFIRMED and the verdict HOLDS. The HOLDS it seals is then weaker, and the plan compares nothing that sees it. Require, per step, the check names in refutations' attempted, survived, counterexamples, errored and not_applicable, plus the response's read, compared through the same canonical form. Band values may move under a side swap (actual and claimed exchange), so name those changes rather than failing on them. Plant a verifier whose refutation set changes while its status does not, and show the audit reports it. My prototype found no such change today over 1,680 key-reordered cases, 30 swaps and 186 whitespace variants, so this adds no noise.

THE AUDIT, the exit rule: (1) It exits only on HOLDS/BROKEN flips, so a restatement that turns INCOMPLETE or SYSTEM_ERROR into HOLDS on a case labelled false, or on a tier row whose source asserts not HOLDS, is filed as a want. That is a false positive reachable by restating the claim, the one failure the moat forbids. Require exit 1 on any restated HOLDS that the label or the row's assertion says is wrong, and list every other change into HOLDS first among the wants. (2) The plan has no path for a flip that exists in today's engine. The tool would exit 1, a suite or slow test requiring exit 0 goes red, the baseline may only shrink, and so the step cannot land and the record cannot be made. My int-to-float prototype found two such flips (first finding). Require the rule now: for example, a pinned list of known flips, each with its filed next run, which the tests assert the tool reports exactly (a new flip fails), while the tool still exits 1. (3) The TRM report says a HOLDS-to-BROKEN flip blocks deployment; the plan names no mechanism (no ship path or CI job that a flip turns red). Name it, or state that this run does not wire the block.

THE AUDIT, coverage: the goal (and the TRM report: 'for each V3 domain ... renamed variables, rescaled units and reordered terms') is an audit of every domain's verifiers. Measured at 06a78d2, only mathematics gets a restatement that changes a verifier's input in a meaning-relevant way: the 30 equality swaps and 186 whitespace variants. Id renaming never reaches a verifier and literal rewriting has no type source (both above). Key reordering reaches the verifiers, since nothing puts packets in canonical order before run_for_domain (verifiers/__init__.py:216-231), and 1,680 cases restated give 0 changes. So the audit can report 0 flips over 1,796 cases while auditing almost no domain beyond key order. Require a per-domain coverage table: cases restated with an input the verifier had not seen, by restatement. The record states plainly which domains only key reordering covers. Either add the report's own restatements where an oracle exists (renamed variables with the variables list, reordered commutative terms), or narrow the goal's claim to what is covered. Also say how tier rows whose source path is audit.audit(text) are audited, since packet restatements cannot pass through text: declined with a reason, or run through verify_derivation.

findings: THE RESTATEMENTS, R4's oracle passes two meaning changes. (1) Defaulted symbol parameters. derivative, integral, limit, solve and inequality read spec.get('variable', 'x') (mathematics.py:313, :336, :359, :384, :424), and all 14 benchmark inequality claims omit 'variable' (they carry 'variables', which verify_inequality never reads). So renaming x in lhs and rhs leaves the verifier solving over x. The oracle cannot see this: 'parse trees equal under the symbol map, new names fresh, absent from every parameter' holds, because the default is not in the packet. Measured at 06a78d2 on the two symbolic inequality claims ((x-3)**2 > 0 and sin(x) <= 0.9999, both labelled false): x -> v0 with the default left in place turns BROKEN into INCOMPLETE; with variable: 'v0' added, both stay BROKEN. (2) Names sympy reads as something else. 'Fresh' does not exclude them: sympify('E') is Euler's number, and I, N, S, O, Q, beta, gamma, zeta and pi are likewise not plain symbols (measured). Python's ast gives a Name node either way, so the parse-tree oracle passes x -> E. Require R4 to map every symbol-naming parameter per mode: variable (written in explicitly when it was defaulted), variables, system's claimed_solution keys (:839-840), and anything else a mode reads as a symbol, declining a mode it cannot map. Draw new names from a fixed pattern that sympify(name) returns as Symbol(name) with no locals. Plant both mistakes and show the oracle declines them.

GATES, the src/ pin: 'a test pins that no module under src/ imports or mentions restate or restatement_audit' is red at the base if 'mentions' is matched without regard to case. src/concordance/verifiers/law.py:45 and :75 cite the 'Restatement (Second) of Contracts', and this run may not change src/, so the step could never pass. Pin what the boundary is: no module under src/ imports or loads tools/restate.py or tools/restatement_audit.py (no import of restate or restatement_audit, no spec_from_file_location naming either path), checked by parsing each module's imports and string constants for those two module names or paths, and shown to pass on law.py.

RECORDED, the frame_seq gap: MEASURED.md is to name the pressure_fighting type-as-BROKEN finding 'with its source (checker-26's prototype)'. That source is a scratch script outside the repository, and CLAUDE.md requires every number in MEASURED.md to come from a tool in tools/, with the section's own test recomputing every quoted number. Either back the gap with a test in this run that recomputes it (the two named cases with frame_seq 1 -> 1.0 read BROKEN, citing pressure_fighting.py:92), or name it in MEASURED.md without a count, pointing to the filed run that will measure it.

It runs under halt_telemetry's isolation (imported), warms first, re-measures a timeout once. It reports every change and every decline by domain, by restatement and by case, plus a per-domain coverage table (restatements applied and declined per domain, naming the domains reached only by R1). Exit 1 on any HOLDS/BROKEN flip, or any change from not-HOLDS to HOLDS on a case labelled false or a tier row whose source asserts not HOLDS; exit 2 if it measured nothing; else 0.

KNOWN FLIPS, PINNED: if the audit finds any exit-1 change in today's engine, it is listed in a KNOWN table in the tool with its filed fixing run, the tool still exits 1, and the tests require the measured set of exit-1 changes to equal KNOWN exactly - so a new one fails the suite and a fixed one must be removed; the lead's rule (no V3 ship in that domain until its run lands) is recorded in the ledger for each entry.

text: WANT (found by checker-28 probing R4, round 2, outside the audit's population): the mathematics verifier compares a sign-ambiguous polynomial gcd or lcm exactly, so its verdict depends on symbol names. sympy picks the sign by the alphabetical order of the symbols: gcd(y - x, x - y) = x - y reads HOLDS, and after renaming x and y it reads BROKEN; gcd(y**2 - x**2, x - y) = x - y likewise; lcm(y - x, x - y) = x - y goes from BROKEN to HOLDS. A gcd is defined only up to a unit, so the claim means the same under the rename, and the two verdicts cannot both be right. That makes it a potential false positive. DECISION (lead): gcd and lcm stay in R4's function list; the oracle is not narrowed to hide a verifier defect. No benchmark case or tier row contains gcd( or lcm( today, so no measured number changes and KNOWN does not list it (KNOWN covers the audit's population). Until a fixing run lands, the lead ships no V3 change to the mathematics verifier's gcd and lcm handling, under the same hold the plan sets for flips the audit finds. Filed as its own run in the loop.
